subject: Orthopedics
stem: A fall on the outstretched hand causes a fracture of the radial shaft at the junction of its middle and distal thirds with dislocation of the distal radio-ulnar joint. This is
explanation: Remember it as **GRUM**: Galeazzi is a Radius fracture with Ulnar (distal) dislocation; Monteggia is an Ulnar fracture with radial head dislocation. Both need open reduction and internal fixation of the shaft fracture.
exam: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (fall on outstretched hand with radial shaft fracture at junction — Galeazzi fracture, 6X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Monteggia fracture-dislocation consists of
options: Fracture of the radial shaft with distal radio-ulnar dislocation
Fracture of the distal radius with ulnar styloid avulsion
Fracture of the proximal ulna with anterior dislocation of the radial head
explanation: The Bado classification grades it by the direction of radial head displacement. A missed radial head dislocation is the classic error, so the elbow must be imaged in every forearm fracture.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (Galeazzi fracture, 6X), 2014 AIIMS (forearm fracture patterns)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The commonest fractured bone of the wrist, and the part of it most liable to avascular necrosis, are
explanation: Blood supply enters distally and runs retrograde, so a proximal fragment loses its supply. Tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox with a normal initial radiograph warrants immobilisation and repeat imaging or MRI.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (most common bone fracture in wrist — scaphoid), 2018 AIIMS (part of scaphoid most susceptible to avascular necrosis — proximal 1/3)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The bone that does **not** take part in forming the wrist joint is the
explanation: The radiocarpal joint is formed by the distal radius and the articular disc with the scaphoid, lunate and triquetrum. The ulna articulates with the carpus only indirectly through the triangular fibrocartilage complex.
exam: 2020 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (bone not taking part in formation of wrist joint — ulna, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The first carpal bone to ossify is the
explanation: Capitate and hamate ossify at about 2 to 3 months, and the pisiform last at about 9 to 12 years. Carpal ossification sequence is used for bone age estimation in children.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (first carpal bone to ossify — capitate)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A child has a supracondylar fracture of the humerus. The three bony point relationship is
options: Lost, because the joint is disrupted
Maintained, because the fracture is proximal to the elbow joint
explanation: The olecranon, medial and lateral epicondyles keep their equilateral triangle. The relationship is **lost in elbow dislocation**, which is the whole point of the test.
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (three bony point relationship maintained in supracondylar fracture of humerus, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The vessel most at risk in a supracondylar fracture of the humerus is the
explanation: The sharp proximal fragment of an extension-type fracture threatens it anteriorly. Untreated ischaemia causes Volkmann contracture, so pulses and capillary refill are documented before and after every reduction.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG / 2016 AIIMS (vessel affected in supracondylar fracture of humerus — brachial artery, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Cubitus varus or gun-stock deformity follows
options: Lateral condyle fracture of the humerus
Malunited supracondylar fracture of the humerus
explanation: Medial tilt of the distal fragment produces it. A **lateral condyle** fracture that malunites or fails to unite instead produces cubitus **valgus**, which stretches the ulnar nerve over time.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (cubitus varus or gun stock deformity caused by supracondylar fracture, 3X), 2021 NEET-PG (cubitus varus deformity)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A child treated for a lateral condyle fracture of the humerus gradually develops an elbow deformity and later cannot adduct the fingers. The mechanism is
options: Cubitus varus causing radial nerve palsy
Cubitus valgus causing tardy ulnar nerve palsy
explanation: The valgus deformity stretches the ulnar nerve behind the medial epicondyle over years. Loss of finger adduction reflects palmar interossei weakness. Anterior transposition of the nerve is the treatment.
exam: 2024 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (lateral condyle fracture with gradual elbow deformity — inability to adduct fingers from tardy ulnar nerve palsy, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A lateral condyle fracture of the humerus in a child is managed by
options: Open reduction and internal fixation, because it is an intra-articular Salter–Harris IV injury
Closed reduction and cast in all cases
explanation: Crossing the physis and the joint surface means that any displacement risks non-union, growth disturbance and progressive valgus. Displaced fractures therefore need anatomical fixation.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (lateral condylar fracture of humerus is managed by open reduction — true), 2014 AIIMS (supracondylar fracture — Salter Harris type 4 classification)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A maid lifted a toddler by the forearms and the child now refuses to use the arm, holding it pronated. The diagnosis is
explanation: Longitudinal traction on a pronated forearm slips the annular ligament over the radial head. Supination with flexion reduces it, often with an audible click, and radiographs are normal.
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (maid rotated child by holding forearms, child started crying — pulled elbow)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Regarding anterior shoulder dislocation, which statement is TRUE?
options: The radial nerve is most often injured
It is the commonest type, and the axillary nerve is the most commonly injured nerve
It is associated with internal rotation deformity
explanation: Over 95% are anterior, with the arm held abducted and externally rotated. Sensation over the deltoid is tested before and after reduction. Posterior dislocation is associated with seizures and electrocution.
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (anterior shoulder dislocation is MC type, axillary nerve most commonly injured, 4X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A Bankart lesion is
options: An avulsion of the greater tuberosity
A compression fracture of the posterolateral humeral head
Injury to the anteroinferior glenoid labrum
explanation: A **Hill–Sachs** lesion is the paired humeral head impression fracture. Both predispose to recurrent dislocation, and a bony Bankart lesion involves the glenoid rim.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (Bankart lesion is injury to anterior inferior glenoid labrum)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Injury to the axillary nerve can result from
options: Fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus or shoulder dislocation
explanation: The nerve winds round the surgical neck in the quadrangular space. Deltoid paralysis with loss of sensation over the regimental badge area results; abduction beyond the first 15 degrees is lost.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (injury to axillary nerve due to fracture of surgical neck of humerus, shoulder dislocation)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A spiral fracture of the humeral shaft characteristically injures the
options: Radial nerve in the spiral groove
explanation: Wrist drop with preserved triceps function results, because triceps branches arise proximally. Most are neuropraxic and recover, so expectant management with a cock-up splint is usual.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (spiral fracture of shaft of humerus can cause injury to radial nerve)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Ligaments disrupted in acromioclavicular joint dislocation are the
explanation: The Rockwood classification grades injury by the degree of disruption and displacement. Grades I and II are treated conservatively; higher grades in active patients may need reconstruction.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (ligaments disrupted in acromioclavicular joint dislocation)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Popeye sign indicates
options: Rupture of the long head of the biceps tendon
explanation: Distal migration of the muscle belly produces the bulge. It usually follows chronic degeneration in older patients and is often managed conservatively, as elbow flexion is preserved by the short head and brachialis.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (Popeye's sign represents long head of biceps tendon rupture)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: In painful arc syndrome, pain is felt during
explanation: Subacromial impingement of the supraspinatus tendon and bursa against the acromion causes it. Neer and Hawkins tests reproduce it, and a subacromial injection relieving pain confirms the diagnosis.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (in painful arc syndrome, pain is felt during mid abduction)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The treatment of choice for an irreparable rotator cuff tear in a young patient is
explanation: Latissimus dorsi transfer is used for posterosuperior tears and pectoralis major for anterosuperior tears. **Reverse** shoulder arthroplasty is reserved for older patients with cuff tear arthropathy.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (treatment of choice for irreparable tear of rotator cuff in a young patient — tendon transfer)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Mallet finger is characterised by
options: Flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joint with extension of the DIP
Flexion deformity of the distal interphalangeal joint from extensor tendon avulsion at its insertion
Inability to flex the DIP joint
explanation: It is treated with an extension splint for 6 to 8 weeks. **Jersey finger** is the counterpart injury — avulsion of flexor digitorum profundus, so the DIP cannot be actively flexed.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (mallet finger characterised by PIP extension and DIP flexion), 2017 AIIMS (flexion of DIP joint — mallet finger), 2015 AIIMS (jersey finger from flexor digitorum profundus rupture, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Hyperextension at the metacarpophalangeal joint with flexion at the interphalangeal joints indicates loss of
explanation: The intrinsics flex the MCP joints and extend the IP joints through the extensor expansion, so their loss reverses both — the intrinsic-minus or claw position.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (hyperextension at MCP with flexion at IP joint — lumbricals)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Madelung deformity is characterised by
options: Dorsal subluxation of the ulna after Colles fracture
Radial deviation of the hand with absent radius
Volar and ulnar deviation of the hand from premature fusion of the volar-ulnar distal radial physis
Fixed flexion of the fingers from palmar fascia contracture
explanation: It is associated with Léri–Weill dyschondrosteosis and Turner syndrome, and presents in adolescent girls. Option D describes Dupuytren contracture.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (match the following — Madelung deformity with volar and ulnar deviation of hand)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: After a road traffic accident a patient has severe left hip pain with the limb held in flexion, adduction and internal rotation. The diagnosis is
explanation: Posterior dislocation is far commoner, typically from a dashboard injury, and the limb is shortened. **Anterior** dislocation holds the limb in abduction, external rotation and slight flexion — the mirror image.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (posterior dislocation of hip — flexion, adduction, internal rotation, 2X), 2024 INI-CET (RTA with hip pain — anterior dislocation of hip, 4X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The nerve most at risk in posterior dislocation of the hip is the
explanation: It lies directly behind the joint, and the common peroneal division is most vulnerable, causing foot drop. Dislocation is reduced urgently to limit both nerve injury and avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (nerve injury is more common in anterior hip dislocation compared to posterior — false)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 75-year-old man has an intracapsular fracture of the femoral neck. The treatment of choice is
explanation: The retrograde blood supply through the retinacular vessels is disrupted, so union and head survival are poor in the elderly. Replacement allows early mobilisation. Internal fixation is preferred in young patients to preserve the head.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (treatment for intracapsular fracture of femur neck in a 75-year-old — hemiarthroplasty)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 60-year-old has a limping gait with left hip pain and radiographs showing a sclerosed irregular femoral head with preserved joint space. The diagnosis is
options: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head
explanation: Preserved joint space with subchondral sclerosis and the crescent sign distinguishes it early. MRI is the most sensitive investigation. Steroids, alcohol, sickle cell disease, trauma and caisson disease are the causes.
exam: 2023 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (60-year-old with limping gait, sclerosed irregular femoral head — avascular necrosis of femur, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The gold standard treatment for a closed fracture of the femoral shaft in an adult is
explanation: A load-sharing device in the mechanical axis allows early weight-bearing and gives high union rates. Reaming raises a theoretical fat embolism risk, and the operation is best done within the first 24 hours in a stable patient.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (gold standard treatment for fracture shaft of femur in adults — intramedullary nailing, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: An **open** fracture of the femoral shaft with significant contamination is best managed by
options: Immediate intramedullary nailing in all cases
explanation: Thorough debridement, antibiotics and tetanus cover come first; external fixation avoids placing a large implant in a contaminated medullary canal. Definitive internal fixation follows once the wound is clean.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (treatment of open fracture of femur — open reduction and external fixation)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Gustilo–Anderson type IIIB open fracture is defined by
options: Extensive soft tissue loss requiring flap coverage, with periosteal stripping, but intact vascularity
A wound of 1 to 10 cm with moderate soft tissue damage
explanation: Type IIIC adds an arterial injury needing repair and carries the worst prognosis. The grading drives antibiotic choice, timing of coverage and amputation decisions.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (Gustilo Anderson injury type 3b — open wound >10 cm with extensive injury requiring soft tissue coverage)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A pelvic fracture with bleeding and shock is immediately managed by
options: Applying a circumferential pelvic binder, such as a sheet tied around the pelvis
explanation: It reduces pelvic volume and tamponades venous bleeding at the level of the greater trochanters. Massive transfusion, then angioembolisation or pelvic packing, follow. Pelvic fracture is a major cause of exsanguination in blunt trauma.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (pelvic fracture with bleeding and shock — tie a bedsheet around the pelvis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Judet view radiograph is used to assess
explanation: Judet oblique (iliac and obturator) views demonstrate the anterior and posterior columns. CT with three-dimensional reconstruction has largely superseded them but the eponym is still examined.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (Judet view of X-ray is used for acetabular fractures, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A patient with chronic knee pain and no trauma has radiographs showing a fragmented patella. The appropriate advice is
options: Radiograph the other knee, as this is likely a bipartite patella
explanation: Bipartite patella is a developmental variant, usually superolateral and often bilateral, with smooth corticated margins. Absence of trauma and bilaterality distinguish it from a fracture.
exam: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG / 2014 AIIMS (chronic knee pain, no trauma, patellar fragmentation — bipartite patella, advise X-ray of other knee, 4X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A displaced transverse fracture of the patella is managed by
explanation: It converts the distracting pull of the quadriceps into a compressive force across the fracture, allowing early movement. Undisplaced fractures with an intact extensor mechanism are treated conservatively.
exam: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (fracture of patella managed by tension band wiring, 4X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: An impact on the **medial** aspect of the knee produces
explanation: A medial blow forces the knee into varus, stretching the structures on the opposite (lateral) side. A **lateral** blow causes valgus and injures the medial collateral ligament, often with the ACL and medial meniscus — the unhappy triad.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (impact on medial aspect of knee results in lateral collateral ligament injury)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The posterior cruciate ligament
options: Is the main restraint to internal rotation
Arises from the posterior tibial plateau and attaches to the lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle
Prevents anterior translation of the tibia
explanation: It prevents **posterior** tibial translation, tested by the posterior drawer and sag signs. The ACL is the primary restraint to anterior translation and contributes to rotational control.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (PCL arises from posterior aspect of tibial plateau), 2018 AIIMS (PCL is the main restraint to internal rotation — false)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A fracture of the base of the fifth metatarsal is immobilised in a below-knee cast for
explanation: An avulsion of the tuberosity by peroneus brevis usually unites well. A **Jones fracture** at the metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction is in a watershed zone and often needs screw fixation because of non-union risk.
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (fracture of base of fifth metatarsal — below knee POP cast for 6–8 weeks, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: March fracture refers to a stress fracture of the
explanation: Repetitive loading in soldiers and runners causes it. Early radiographs are often normal and **MRI is the investigation of choice** for a suspected stress fracture; callus later confirms it.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (march fracture seen in neck of second metatarsal), 2015 AIIMS (investigation of choice in stress fracture — MRI)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A young marathon runner has pain over the anteromedial border of the tibia on running. The diagnosis is
options: Stress fracture of the femoral neck
explanation: It is an overuse periostitis along the posteromedial tibial border, relieved by rest and load modification. Persistent focal pain with night symptoms needs MRI to exclude a tibial stress fracture.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (young marathon runner with pain on anterior and medial tibia — shin splints)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A Pilon fracture is
options: An avulsion of the medial malleolus
A fracture of the tibial tuberosity
A comminuted intra-articular fracture of the distal tibia
explanation: Axial loading drives the talus into the tibial plafond. Soft tissue swelling is severe, so staged management with spanning external fixation followed by definitive fixation is standard.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (match the following — Pilon fracture is comminuted intra-articular fracture of distal tibia)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The bony tuberosity on the anterior aspect of the upper end of the tibia is the
options: Tibial tuberosity, the insertion of the patellar tendon
explanation: Traction apophysitis here in an adolescent is Osgood–Schlatter disease. **Gerdy tubercle** is the lateral tibial site of iliotibial band insertion and is avulsed in Segond fracture.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (bony tuberosity on anterior aspect of upper end of tibia — tibial tuberosity)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Triple arthrodesis involves fusion of the
explanation: It corrects hindfoot deformity and gives a stable, painless foot in polio, neglected clubfoot and arthritis. The **ankle joint itself is preserved**, so dorsiflexion and plantarflexion remain.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (triple arthrodesis involves talonavicular joint, calcaneocuboid joint, subtalar joint)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The talocalcaneonavicular joint is a
explanation: The talar head sits in a socket formed by the navicular, the spring ligament and the calcaneal facets, permitting inversion and eversion. The ankle (talocrural) joint itself is a hinge.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (talocalcaneonavicular joint is a ball and socket joint)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A deformity in which the great toe deviates laterally is
explanation: A medial bunion forms over the first metatarsal head. Narrow footwear, female sex and a positive family history predispose. Hallux rigidus is instead first metatarsophalangeal osteoarthritis with restricted dorsiflexion.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (deformity in which great toe is deviated laterally — hallux valgus)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Haglund deformity affects which region?
options: The posterosuperior calcaneum at the ankle, causing retrocalcaneal bursitis
explanation: A prominent calcaneal bump impinges against the Achilles tendon and shoe counter, producing the "pump bump". Footwear modification, physiotherapy and sometimes surgical resection are used.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (Haglund deformity is seen in ankle joint)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Reduced angle between the neck and shaft of the femur is
explanation: The normal neck-shaft angle is about 125 to 135 degrees. Coxa vara shortens the limb and produces a Trendelenburg gait; rickets, fibrous dysplasia, slipped epiphysis and malunion cause it.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (reduced angle between neck and shaft of femur — coxa vara), 2017 AIIMS (identify the deformity — coxa vara)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Shenton line is assessed on a radiograph of the
explanation: It is a smooth curve from the inferior border of the femoral neck to the inferior margin of the superior pubic ramus. Disruption indicates femoral neck fracture, developmental dysplasia or slipped capital femoral epiphysis.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (Shenton's line is seen in X-ray of hip)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A patient cannot move the fourth and fifth digits and cannot hold a sheet of paper between the fingers. The likely fracture site is the
explanation: The ulnar nerve runs behind the medial epicondyle. Loss of the card test reflects palmar interossei weakness, and Froment sign reflects adductor pollicis weakness with compensatory flexor pollicis longus action.
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (unable to move 4th and 5th digit, cannot hold paper — medial condyle of humerus, ulnar nerve injury, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Claw hand involving the ring and little fingers indicates injury to the
explanation: The ulnar nerve supplies the medial two lumbricals, so only the ring and little fingers claw. A **combined** ulnar and median injury produces a complete claw hand affecting all four fingers.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (claw hand involving ring and little finger — ulnar nerve injury)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A cock-up splint is used for
explanation: It holds the wrist in extension to overcome wrist drop and restore a functional grip while the nerve recovers. A **knuckle-bender** splint is used for ulnar palsy and an opponens splint for median palsy.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG / 2020 INI-CET (cock up splint is used for radial nerve palsy, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Injury to the neck of the fibula causes
options: Tibial nerve palsy with loss of plantarflexion
Common peroneal nerve palsy with foot drop and a steppage gait
Sciatic nerve palsy with complete paralysis
explanation: The nerve winds superficially round the fibular neck, so it is vulnerable to fracture, tight plaster and prolonged squatting. Dorsiflexion and eversion are lost with sensory loss over the dorsum of the foot.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (injury to neck of fibula leads to steppage gait), 2022 INI-CET (nerve injured in neck of fibula fracture — common peroneal nerve), 2018 AIIMS (foot drop caused by common peroneal nerve)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: When a patient bears weight on the right lower limb the left pelvis drops. The lesion is
explanation: A positive Trendelenburg sign indicates failure of the **stance-side** abductors. The superior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus medius and minimus, which abduct and internally rotate the hip and stabilise the pelvis.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (bearing weight on right lower limb, left pelvis dropped — right superior gluteal nerve palsy, 2X), 2022 INI-CET (Trendelenburg gait — gluteus medius)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The muscle action tested by the Trendelenburg mechanism is
explanation: Gluteus medius and minimus perform both. A positive test also occurs in coxa vara, hip dislocation, avascular necrosis and any painful hip, so it is not specific to nerve injury.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (muscle action tested in Trendelenburg mechanism — abduction and external rotation, recorded loosely)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A nerve injury in which the axon is disrupted but the nerve sheath remains intact is
explanation: Wallerian degeneration follows, then regeneration at about 1 mm per day along the intact sheath, so recovery is slow but possible. **Neurapraxia** is a conduction block with recovery in weeks; **neurotmesis** divides the sheath and needs repair.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (nerve injury with intact nerve sheath — axonotmesis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: In polio, a hand-knee gait results from weakness of the
explanation: Without active knee extension the patient presses on the thigh with the hand to stabilise the knee in stance. Quadriceps weakness also gives a positive Hoover and a hand-to-knee gait pattern.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (in polio, hand-knee gait is due to weakness of quadriceps)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Numbness and tingling of the lateral three digits with nocturnal symptoms indicates
options: Carpal tunnel syndrome, confirmed by the Durkan test
explanation: Median nerve compression beneath the flexor retinaculum. Durkan carpal compression is more sensitive than Tinel or Phalen signs. Pregnancy, hypothyroidism, diabetes, acromegaly and rheumatoid arthritis predispose.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (numbness and tingling in lateral 3 digits — carpal tunnel syndrome, Durkan test)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The pen test assesses
options: Median nerve function, through abductor pollicis brevis
explanation: The patient abducts the thumb to touch a pen held above the hand; failure indicates thenar weakness. The **book test** assesses ulnar function by testing adductor pollicis grip strength.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (pen test is used to assess median nerve), 2020 INI-CET (book test is done for ulnar nerve testing)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Erb palsy involves which nerve roots, and what is the characteristic posture?
options: C8 and T1; a claw hand
C5 and C6; the arm adducted and internally rotated with the forearm pronated — a waiter's tip deformity
C5 to T1; a flail arm
explanation: It follows excessive traction on the shoulder, as in shoulder dystocia. **Klumpke palsy** involves C8 and T1, gives a claw hand and may include Horner syndrome from T1 sympathetic involvement.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (axillary nerve injury), 2023 INI-CET (claw hand from ulnar nerve injury)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Winging of the scapula results from injury to the
options: Long thoracic nerve, paralysing serratus anterior
explanation: It is commonly injured during axillary dissection. Serratus anterior protracts the scapula and holds it against the chest wall, so its loss prevents full overhead abduction.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (axillary nerve injury), 2022 INI-CET (superior gluteal nerve palsy, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Meralgia paraesthetica is caused by entrapment of the
options: Femoral nerve in the femoral canal
Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh beneath the inguinal ligament
Common peroneal nerve at the fibular neck
explanation: Burning anterolateral thigh pain with no motor weakness results. Obesity, tight belts, pregnancy and iliac crest bone graft harvesting are the causes, and it is purely sensory.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (nerve injured at neck of fibula), 2018 AIIMS (foot drop from common peroneal nerve)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The earliest clinical sign of nerve recovery after repair is
options: Return of an advancing Tinel sign along the nerve
explanation: Tapping over the regenerating axon tips produces tingling in its distribution, and the point of maximal response advances distally at about 1 mm per day. Motor recovery comes much later.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (axonotmesis with intact nerve sheath), 2018 NEET-PG (carpal tunnel syndrome and Durkan test)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Thomas test is performed to detect
options: Fixed flexion deformity (flexion contracture) of the hip
explanation: Lumbar lordosis masks hip flexion deformity, so the opposite hip is flexed to flatten the spine and reveal it. It is one of the most repeated clinical tests in the subject.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (test done in cases of hip flexion contracture — Thomas test), 2017 AIIMS (test done for hip flexor contracture — Thomas test), 2015 AIIMS (identify the test — Thomas test)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The correct sequence of the Thomas test is
options: Abduct the hip then adduct it
Flex both hips simultaneously then extend
Square the pelvis, flex the normal hip to obliterate lordosis, then observe the opposite thigh rising off the couch
Internally rotate the hip in extension
explanation: The angle between the thigh and the couch measures the fixed flexion deformity. Squaring the pelvis first is essential, or an apparent deformity may simply be pelvic tilt.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (sequence of Thomas test — squaring of pelvis, flexion of hip, overcorrection)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The McMurray test detects
explanation: The knee is flexed then extended with rotation and valgus or varus stress, seeking a click or pain. Apley grinding and Thessaly tests are alternatives, and MRI is the imaging investigation of choice.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (test used to detect meniscal tear — McMurray test)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Finkelstein test involves which tendons?
options: Flexor pollicis longus and flexor carpi radialis
Extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis
Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
Extensor carpi radialis brevis and longus
explanation: These occupy the first extensor compartment in de Quervain tenosynovitis. Ulnar deviation of the wrist with the thumb held in the palm reproduces the pain. It is common in new mothers and racquet players.
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (tendons involved in Finkelstein's test — APL and EPB), 2014 AIIMS (de Quervain tenosynovitis involves extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Roos (elevated arm stress) test is used to diagnose
explanation: The arms are held abducted and externally rotated while the hands open and close for 3 minutes, reproducing symptoms. Adson test is the alternative; a cervical rib may be the cause.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (Roos test is done to diagnose thoracic outlet syndrome)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Allen test is performed to
options: Confirm collateral flow through the ulnar artery before radial artery cannulation
explanation: Both arteries are occluded, then the ulnar released; colour should return within about 5 to 10 seconds. Adequate collateral supply is what makes the radial artery safe to cannulate or harvest.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (Allen test is used to check patency of ulnar artery before radial artery cannulation)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Hoover sign is used to
options: Detect feigned or non-organic lower limb weakness, by feeling for involuntary heel pressure on the opposite side
explanation: The examiner cups both heels; genuine effort to lift one leg produces downward pressure from the other. Its absence suggests the patient is not truly trying.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (examiner keeps hands under the heels in supine position — Hoover sign)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Ortolani and Barlow manoeuvres are used to detect
options: Developmental dysplasia of the hip in a newborn
explanation: Barlow **dislocates** a dislocatable hip and Ortolani **relocates** a dislocated one. Narath sign is the additional recorded sign. Ultrasound is used for confirmation, as radiographs are unhelpful before ossification.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (signs seen in cases of DDH — Ortolani, Barlow, Narath)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A positive Trendelenburg test indicates
options: Failure of the abductors on the non-weight-bearing side
Failure of the hip abductors on the weight-bearing side
explanation: The pelvis drops on the **unsupported** side, which is the commonest point of confusion in this question. Any painful or unstable hip, as well as abductor paralysis, produces it.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (weight bearing on right lower limb with left pelvis dropping, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The Lachman test assesses
options: The anterior cruciate ligament, and is more sensitive than the anterior drawer test
explanation: It is performed at about 20 to 30 degrees of flexion, where hamstring spasm interferes least. The pivot-shift test assesses rotational instability and is the most specific.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (McMurray test for meniscal tear), 2024 INI-CET (PCL anatomy)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Gaenslen and FABER (Patrick) tests are used to assess
explanation: FABER stands for flexion, abduction and external rotation. Sacroiliac stress tests are central to assessing inflammatory back pain, as in ankylosing spondylitis.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (ankylosing spondylitis with sacroiliac involvement), 2017 AIIMS (Thomas test)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The straight leg raising test is positive when pain radiates down the leg between
options: 30 and 70 degrees of hip flexion, indicating lumbar nerve root tension
Any range, which is always abnormal
explanation: Below 30 degrees the nerve roots are not yet stretched, and beyond 70 degrees hamstring tightness confounds it. A positive **crossed** straight leg raise is more specific for disc herniation.
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (lower backache radiating to right leg — S1 root), 2024 INI-CET (cauda equina syndrome)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Apparent and true limb length are distinguished because
options: Both are measured from the umbilicus
True length is measured from the anterior superior iliac spine to the medial malleolus, and apparent length from the xiphisternum or umbilicus
explanation: Apparent shortening with normal true length indicates pelvic tilt from adduction deformity. Galeazzi and Bryant tests localise shortening above or below the knee.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (Thomas test sequence and squaring of pelvis), 2021 INI-CET (coxa vara)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Intra-articular fractures are characterised by
options: Pain on both active and passive movement
explanation: Any movement displaces the fractured articular surfaces. Pain only on **active** movement suggests a muscle or tendon lesion, which is the discriminating principle.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (intra-articular fractures — active and passive movements are painful)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Inflammatory arthritis is distinguished from degenerative arthritis by
options: Pain worse with activity and relieved by rest
Morning stiffness lasting over an hour, raised ESR, joint swelling and juxta-articular rarefaction
Asymmetrical large joint involvement with osteophytes
explanation: Inflammatory pain improves with use, whereas degenerative pain worsens with it. Radiographs show periarticular osteopenia and erosions rather than osteophytes and subchondral sclerosis.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (inflammatory arthritis — morning stiffness, elevated ESR, swelling of joints, rarefaction)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Measurement of the angle of a scoliotic curve on radiograph is known as
explanation: It is measured between the end vertebrae of the curve. Above 20 degrees warrants bracing and above 45 to 50 degrees surgery in a growing child. Boehler angle assesses the calcaneum.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (angle of scoliosis is known as Cobb's angle)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 22-year-old woman has a lytic lesion at the distal radius with a soap-bubble appearance reaching the subarticular region. The diagnosis is
explanation: An eccentric epiphyseal-to-metaphyseal lytic lesion with a distinct margin extending to subarticular bone in a skeletally mature patient. Distal femur, proximal tibia and distal radius are the usual sites.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (22-year-old with lytic lesion at distal radius — giant cell tumour), 2022 INI-CET (soap bubble appearance in distal epiphysis — GCT), 2015 AIIMS (identify the diagnosis — giant cell tumour, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Giant cell tumour of bone is characterised by
options: Diaphyseal location with onion-skin periosteal reaction
A central lytic lesion with a fallen fragment
Epiphyseal-to-metaphyseal location, a distinct margin and eccentric expansion, with multinucleate giant cells on a mononuclear stromal background
explanation: The **mononuclear stromal cell** is the proliferating neoplastic component; the giant cells are reactive. Denosumab, an anti-RANKL antibody, is used in unresectable disease.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (GCT — epiphyseal to metaphyseal location, distinct margin, eccentric), 2024 INI-CET (osteoclast giant cell constitutes the proliferative component — false, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The standard treatment of a giant cell tumour of bone is
options: Extended curettage with adjuvant and bone grafting or cement filling
explanation: Simple curettage recurs in up to half of cases, so the cavity is extended with a burr and treated with phenol, hydrogen peroxide or cement. Immunohistochemistry is used where the histology is equivocal.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (match the following — GCT curettage), 2020 INI-CET (lytic lesion in lower third of femur with biopsy — IHC for GCT, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 10-year-old has a swelling in the tibial diaphysis with onion-skin periosteal reaction. The diagnosis is
explanation: Lamellated or onion-peel periosteal reaction in a **diaphyseal** lesion in the first or second decade is characteristic, often with fever and raised inflammatory markers that mimic osteomyelitis. *EWSR1-FLI1* translocation confirms it.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (10-year-old with swelling in tibial diaphysis and periosteal reaction — Ewing sarcoma), 2018 NEET-PG (fever, limb pain, lamellated X-ray — Ewing's sarcoma)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Ewing sarcoma is characterised by
options: Sunray spiculation with a Codman triangle
Involvement of both bone and soft tissue, presentation in the second decade, and small round blue cells that are PAS positive
explanation: CD99 membrane positivity is the immunohistochemical marker. It is highly chemosensitive and radiosensitive, so treatment is chemotherapy with local control by surgery or radiotherapy.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (Ewing sarcoma — affects both bone and soft tissues, seen in second decade, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The peak incidence of osteosarcoma is in the
explanation: It arises at the metaphysis of rapidly growing bone, most often the distal femur, with sunray spiculation and a Codman triangle. A **second peak** occurs in the elderly, arising in Paget disease or irradiated bone.
exam: 2015 AIIMS (peak incidence of osteosarcoma occurs at 2nd decade)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Staging investigations for osteosarcoma include all EXCEPT
options: PET scan as a routine requirement
explanation: Chest CT is essential because the **lung** is the commonest site of metastasis. MRI of the whole bone assesses local extent and skip lesions, and bone scan detects distant bony deposits.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (investigations in osteosarcoma — X-ray of limb, chest X-ray, CT chest, not PET scan)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 14-year-old has a mushroom-like bony tumour at the distal femur. The feature that most suggests malignant transformation is
options: A stalk arising from the metaphysis
A cartilage cap thicker than 2 cm on MRI
explanation: Osteochondroma is the commonest benign bone tumour and points away from the joint. A thick, growing cap, new pain after skeletal maturity or rapid enlargement suggests chondrosarcoma.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (14-year-old with mushroom like tumour in distal femur — 2 cm hyaline cap thickness on MRI, osteochondroma)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The fallen fragment sign is characteristic of
options: Simple (unicameral) bone cyst with a pathological fracture
explanation: A fracture fragment falls to the dependent part of the fluid-filled cavity, confirming that the lesion is cystic. Treatment is intralesional steroid injection or curettage with grafting.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (fallen fragment sign is seen in simple bone cyst), 2021 INI-CET (match — simple bone cyst intralesional injection)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The treatment of an aneurysmal bone cyst is
explanation: It is an expansile, eccentric, blood-filled lesion showing fluid-fluid levels on MRI. It is locally aggressive with a recurrence rate of 20 to 30%, and selective arterial embolisation is used for inaccessible lesions.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (treatment of aneurysmal bone cyst — extended curettage with allograft)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The treatment of choice for osteoid osteoma is
explanation: A small cortical nidus with surrounding sclerosis causes night pain **dramatically relieved by aspirin or NSAIDs** — the diagnostic hallmark. CT-guided ablation has replaced open excision.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (match the following — osteoid osteoma RFA)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 55-year-old man has bone pain and a skull radiograph showing multiple punched-out lytic lesions. The diagnosis is
explanation: Lesions are purely lytic with **no osteoblastic reaction**, so the bone scan is often negative — skeletal survey or whole-body MRI is used instead. Anaemia, renal failure, hypercalcaemia and M-band complete the picture.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (55-year-old with bone pain and skull X-ray showing punched out lesions — multiple myeloma)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Lytic lesions in the limb bones with biopsy showing proliferating histiocytes containing Birbeck granules indicate
explanation: Eosinophilic granuloma is its localised bony form, and vertebral involvement causes vertebra plana. CD1a and S100 positivity confirm it; solitary lesions may be observed or curetted.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (lytic lesions in lower limb bones with fibroblast proliferation — LCH)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Excess teriparatide therapy carries a risk of
explanation: Teriparatide is recombinant PTH 1-34 given intermittently to stimulate bone formation; continuous exposure instead causes resorption. Treatment is limited to about 2 years. Jaw osteonecrosis and atypical fractures belong to **bisphosphonates**.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (teriparatide in excess can cause osteosarcoma)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Chondromyxoid fibroma typically presents as
options: A diaphyseal lesion with onion-skin reaction
An eccentric metaphyseal lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin in an adolescent, commonly in the proximal tibia
A subarticular lesion with soap-bubble appearance
A central lesion with a fallen fragment
explanation: It is a rare benign cartilaginous tumour treated by curettage. The chondroid, myxoid and fibrous lobular pattern on histology is diagnostic.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (identify the diagnosis in adolescent boy — chondromyxoid fibroma)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The commonest malignant bone tumour overall is
explanation: Breast, prostate, lung, thyroid and kidney are the usual primaries, spreading to the axial skeleton through Batson plexus. Prostate metastases are characteristically osteoblastic; the others are predominantly lytic.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (multiple myeloma with punched out skull lesions), 2015 AIIMS (osteosarcoma peak incidence)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Enchondroma differs from chondrosarcoma in that it
options: Causes night pain with cortical breach
Is painless, with no cortical destruction or periosteal reaction, and is commonest in the small bones of the hand
explanation: New pain, cortical thinning, endosteal scalloping or growth suggest malignant change. Multiple enchondromas define Ollier disease, and with soft tissue haemangiomas, Maffucci syndrome.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (osteochondroma with cartilage cap thickness), 2016 AIIMS (chondromyxoid fibroma)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The commonest site of metastasis from osteosarcoma is the
explanation: Spread is haematogenous, which is why chest CT is mandatory at staging and nodal dissection is not performed. Pulmonary metastasectomy can still be curative in selected patients.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (investigations in osteosarcoma — chest X-ray and CT chest), 2015 AIIMS (peak incidence of osteosarcoma)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Osteoporosis is characterised biochemically by
options: Low calcium with high alkaline phosphatase
Normal calcium, phosphate and alkaline phosphatase
Low phosphate with high parathyroid hormone
explanation: Osteoporosis is reduced bone **quantity** with normal mineralisation, so biochemistry is normal — the key contrast with osteomalacia, where calcium and phosphate fall and alkaline phosphatase rises.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG / 2016 AIIMS (osteoporosis is characterised by normal calcium and ALP levels, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Osteoporosis is associated with a raised level of
explanation: It is an osteoclast marker reflecting increased resorption. Urinary hydroxyproline, N-telopeptide and C-telopeptide are the other resorption markers, while osteocalcin and bone-specific alkaline phosphatase mark formation.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (osteoporosis is characterised by raised levels of tartrate resistant acid phosphatase)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The commonest site of an osteoporotic fracture is the
explanation: Vertebral compression fractures are commonest and often silent, found incidentally as loss of height or kyphosis. Hip fractures carry the greatest mortality, and a distal radius fracture is often the first clinical event.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (osteoporotic fracture is usually seen in vertebra)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A fish-mouth or codfish appearance of the vertebrae on radiograph indicates
explanation: Weakened trabeculae allow the nucleus pulposus to indent the endplates. Picture-frame vertebrae indicate Paget disease, and a rugger-jersey spine indicates renal osteodystrophy.
exam: 2014 AIIMS (the given spine is seen in osteoporosis — fish mouth spine)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 75-year-old woman sustains a femoral shaft fracture after a fall in the bathroom. The underlying condition is
explanation: A fracture from a fall from standing height in someone over 50 is by definition a fragility fracture. It warrants DEXA assessment and treatment, since one fragility fracture strongly predicts the next.
exam: 2021 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (75-year-old female with fall and fracture shaft of femur — osteoporosis, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 60-year-old woman with a Colles fracture has a DEXA T-score of −2.8. The drug of choice is
options: Alendronate, with calcium and vitamin D
explanation: Bisphosphonates are first line for postmenopausal osteoporosis. They must be taken fasting with water, sitting upright, because of oesophagitis risk. Jaw osteonecrosis and atypical femoral fracture are the long-term concerns.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (60-year-old with Colles fracture and DEXA — alendronate), 2021 NEET-PG (first line drug for postmenopausal osteoporosis — bisphosphonates)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A DEXA T-score defining osteoporosis is
explanation: Between −1 and −2.5 is osteopenia. The **T**-score compares with a young adult reference and defines the diagnosis; the **Z**-score compares with age-matched peers and is used in children and premenopausal women.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (DEXA scan with Colles fracture — alendronate), 2018 NEET-PG (osteoporosis biochemistry, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A child with bowing of the legs and widening of the wrists has
explanation: Rachitic rosary, Harrison sulcus, delayed fontanelle closure and craniotabes accompany it. Biochemistry shows low or normal calcium, low phosphate, high alkaline phosphatase and high parathyroid hormone.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (child with bowing of legs — vitamin D deficiency)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Cupping, fraying and splaying at the distal radius and ulna on radiograph indicate
explanation: Defective mineralisation widens the physis and deforms the metaphysis. The wrist, knee and costochondral junctions are the sites of fastest growth and so show changes earliest.
exam: 2023 INI-CET / 2015 AIIMS (cupping, fraying and splaying in distal end of radius and ulna — rickets, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Antenatal ultrasound showing multiple long bone fractures suggests
explanation: A type I collagen defect, usually autosomal dominant, with blue sclerae, deafness, dentinogenesis imperfecta and wormian bones. Type II is lethal perinatally. Bisphosphonates reduce fracture rate in childhood.
exam: 2020 NEET-PG (antenatal USG showing multiple fractures of long bones — osteogenesis imperfecta), 2018 AIIMS (identify the disease — osteogenesis imperfecta)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A child has a shepherd's crook deformity of the femur with hyperpigmented skin lesions. The diagnosis is
explanation: Ground-glass medullary lesions with café-au-lait macules having irregular "coast of Maine" borders. A *GNAS* mutation underlies it, and the varus proximal femoral deformity is the shepherd's crook.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (child with shepherd's crook deformity and hyperpigmented skin lesions — fibrous dysplasia)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 14-year-old girl has multiple brown patches, multiple bony swellings and precocious puberty. The diagnosis is
explanation: The triad is polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait macules and endocrinopathy, classically precocious puberty, from a post-zygotic *GNAS* mutation causing mosaicism.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (14-year-old with multiple brown patches, multiple swellings — McCune Albright syndrome)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Osteitis fibrosa cystica is characterised by
options: Normal parathyroid hormone with low calcium
Raised parathyroid hormone with increased osteoclastic activity and generalised bone resorption
explanation: Severe hyperparathyroidism produces brown tumours, subperiosteal resorption of the radial side of the middle phalanges, and a salt-and-pepper skull. "Stones, bones, abdominal groans and psychic moans" summarises it.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (osteitis fibrosa cystica — increased PTH, increased osteoclastic activity, generalised resorption)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Osteomalacia differs from osteoporosis in that it shows
options: Normal biochemistry with reduced bone mass
Defective mineralisation with low calcium and phosphate, high alkaline phosphatase, and Looser zones on radiograph
explanation: Looser zones are pseudofractures. Osteomalacia causes bone **pain and proximal myopathy**, whereas osteoporosis is painless until a fracture occurs — the clinical discriminator.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (osteoporosis with normal calcium and ALP, 2X), 2022 NEET-PG (vitamin D deficiency with bowing of legs)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Acute osteomyelitis is characterised by
options: Painless swelling with early radiographic change
Severe pain, limitation of movement and periosteal reaction appearing after about 10 days
explanation: Radiographs are **normal for the first 10 to 14 days**, so MRI is the early investigation of choice. The metaphysis is affected because its sluggish sinusoidal blood flow favours bacterial seeding.
exam: 2024 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (acute osteomyelitis — severe pain, limitation of movements, periosteal reaction, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: An 18-year-old boy has fever, limb pain and a local rise of temperature with tenderness over the metaphysis. The likely diagnosis is
explanation: *Staphylococcus aureus* is the commonest organism at all ages. Ewing sarcoma is the key differential, as it also presents with fever, pain and raised inflammatory markers — biopsy settles it.
exam: 2020 INI-CET / 2018 NEET-PG (18-year-old with fever, limb pain, local rise of temperature — osteomyelitis, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: In chronic osteomyelitis with a discharging sinus, newly formed bone surrounding dead bone is called
explanation: **Sequestrum** is the dead avascular bone, and a **cloaca** is the opening in the involucrum through which pus escapes to the sinus. Sequestrectomy with saucerisation is the surgical treatment.
exam: 2022 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (low grade fever with discharging sinus, newly formed bone — involucrum, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A Brodie abscess is
options: A localised subacute osteomyelitis with a well-defined lytic cavity surrounded by sclerosis, usually in the tibial metaphysis
explanation: It reflects a balance between organism virulence and host resistance, so systemic features are minimal and night pain predominates — closely mimicking osteoid osteoma.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (identify the condition — Brodie abscess, answer carries a leaked heading)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A child with sickle cell disease has fever and joint pain. The organism most characteristically responsible for osteomyelitis is
explanation: Bowel infarction allows seeding, and functional asplenia impairs clearance of encapsulated organisms. *Staphylococcus aureus* nevertheless remains common even in sickle cell disease, so cover is broad initially.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (fever, joint pain, sickle shaped RBCs — *Salmonella*)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The commonest joint involved in septic arthritis is the
explanation: In **infants**, however, the hip is commonest and more dangerous because intracapsular pressure compromises the femoral head blood supply. Joint aspiration before antibiotics is essential, and drainage is urgent.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (most common joint involved in septic arthritis — knee)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Tom Smith arthritis involves the
options: Epiphysis of the femoral head in infantile septic arthritis of the hip
explanation: Infantile hip sepsis destroys the capital epiphysis and leaves gross deformity with shortening and instability. It is a preventable cause of lifelong disability, so neonatal hip sepsis is an emergency.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (Tom Smith arthritis involves epiphyseal part of head of femur)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The commonest cause of **non-purulent multifocal** osteomyelitis is
explanation: Synovitis, acne, pustulosis, hyperostosis and osteitis — a sterile autoinflammatory condition. Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis is its paediatric counterpart, and cultures are negative, which is the diagnostic clue.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (most common cause of non-purulent multifocal osteomyelitis — SAPHO syndrome)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The commonest pattern of spinal involvement in tuberculosis is
explanation: Two adjacent vertebrae share a segmental artery, so infection straddles the disc and destroys it — unlike tumour, which spares the disc. Progressive collapse gives the gibbus deformity.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (most common pattern of Pott's spine involvement — paradiscal)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A cold abscess in Pott spine is distinguished from a pyogenic abscess by
options: Absence of the local signs of acute inflammation, with gradual painless tracking along fascial planes
explanation: Psoas abscess tracking to the thigh is the classic example. Tuberculosis of the spine is treated medically, with surgery for neurological deficit, instability or severe deformity.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (paradiscal Pott's spine), 2024 INI-CET (acute osteomyelitis features, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Chronic osteomyelitis is best imaged for the extent of sequestrum by
options: CT, with MRI for soft tissue and marrow involvement
explanation: CT best demonstrates dead bone and cortical detail for surgical planning. A sinogram maps the track, and culture from deep tissue rather than sinus swab guides antibiotic choice.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (involucrum in chronic osteomyelitis, 3X), 2016 AIIMS (Brodie abscess)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Symmetrical arthritis involving the wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints and small joints of both hands indicates
explanation: Symmetry, MCP and wrist involvement with sparing of the distal interphalangeal joints is characteristic. Anti-CCP is the most specific antibody, and methotrexate is the anchor drug.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (symmetric arthritis involving bilateral wrist and hands — RA)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Involvement of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints and the first carpometacarpal joint, with sparing of the wrist and metacarpophalangeal joints, indicates
explanation: Hand osteoarthritis spares the MCP joints and wrist — the mirror image of rheumatoid arthritis. Bouchard nodes are at the PIP joints and Heberden nodes at the DIP joints.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (involvement of PIP, DIP, 1st CMC with sparing of wrist and MCP — osteoarthritis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The radiographic hallmark of osteoarthritis is
options: Asymmetrical joint space narrowing with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and cysts
explanation: Osteoarthritis is a **productive** process with new bone formation, whereas inflammatory arthritis is erosive with periarticular osteopenia — the key radiological distinction.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (osteoarthritis hand distribution), 2018 AIIMS (inflammatory arthritis features)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Glucosamine supplementation is used in
options: Rheumatoid arthritis as a disease-modifying drug
Osteoarthritis, as a symptomatic agent with modest and debated benefit
explanation: Weight loss, exercise and quadriceps strengthening have the strongest evidence in knee osteoarthritis, with paracetamol and topical NSAIDs for symptoms and arthroplasty for end-stage disease.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (glucosamine supplementation is given in arthritis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Ankylosing spondylitis is characterised by
options: Distal interphalangeal involvement with nail pitting
Onset after 60 years with female predominance
Onset at 20 to 40 years, male predominance, HLA-B27 positivity and sacroiliac joint involvement
explanation: Inflammatory back pain improving with exercise, reduced chest expansion and a bamboo spine from syndesmophytes are the features. Uveitis, aortitis and apical fibrosis are extra-articular associations.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (ankylosing spondylitis — 20–40 years, males, HLA B27, SI joint involvement)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A Charcot joint is
options: A grossly destroyed, unstable but relatively painless joint resulting from loss of protective sensation
explanation: Diabetes is now the commonest cause, affecting the foot and ankle; tabes dorsalis, syringomyelia and leprosy are the classical ones. The mismatch between gross destruction and minimal pain is diagnostic.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (identify the diagnosis — Charcot joint, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Mseleni joint disease is
options: An endemic osteoarthropathy of northern KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa
explanation: A geographically restricted degenerative joint disease affecting hips and other large joints, with a female predominance. Kashin–Beck disease is the comparable endemic osteoarthropathy of parts of Asia.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (Mseleni joint disease is endemic to northern KwaZulu Natal area in South Africa)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Acute gout is confirmed by
options: Negatively birefringent needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals in joint fluid under polarised light
explanation: Serum urate may be normal during an attack, so it cannot confirm or exclude gout. Rhomboid positively birefringent crystals with chondrocalcinosis indicate **pseudogout** from calcium pyrophosphate.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (symmetric arthritis — RA), 2018 AIIMS (inflammatory arthritis features)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Acute gout in a patient already on allopurinol is managed by
options: Continuing allopurinol and treating the attack with an NSAID, colchicine or steroid
explanation: Stopping or changing urate-lowering therapy during an attack causes urate flux and prolongs it. Conversely, urate-lowering therapy is **started** only under anti-inflammatory cover, since initiation can precipitate a flare.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (rheumatoid arthritis), 2017 AIIMS (glucosamine in arthritis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Total knee replacement in osteoarthritis is indicated when
options: There is severe pain with functional limitation despite adequate conservative management
Radiographic changes appear, regardless of symptoms
The patient is over 60, regardless of symptoms
explanation: Radiographic severity correlates poorly with symptoms, so the **patient**, not the film, is the indication. Active infection, uncorrectable extensor mechanism deficiency and poor rehabilitation potential are contraindications.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (glucosamine supplementation in arthritis), 2022 NEET-PG (hand osteoarthritis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Congenital talipes equinovarus is characterised by
options: Male predominance, frequent bilaterality, and about 90% correction with conservative treatment
explanation: The deformity is CAVE — Cavus, Adductus, Varus, Equinus. The Ponseti method of serial manipulation and casting, with percutaneous tenotomy and bracing, is the standard of care.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (CTEV — more common in males, bilateral, correction rate 90% with conservative treatment, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: CTEV (Dennis Browne) shoes are characterised by
options: No heel, a straight inner border and an outer shoe raise
A raised heel with a curved inner border
explanation: Each feature counteracts one component: the straight inner border opposes forefoot adduction, the outer raise opposes varus, and removing the heel opposes equinus.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (CTEV shoes — no heel, straight inner border, outer shoe raise)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The sequence of surgery in open reduction for developmental dysplasia of the hip is
options: Capsulotomy, locate the acetabulum by tracing the ligamentum teres, excise obstructing tissue, then reduce
explanation: The ligamentum teres reliably leads to the true acetabulum, which may be hard to identify when filled with pulvinar and an inverted limbus. Femoral and pelvic osteotomies are added if reduction is unstable.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (sequence of surgery in DDH — capsulotomy, locate acetabulum by tracing ligamentum teres)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Risk factors for Perthes disease include
options: Male sex, a positive family history and passive smoking
explanation: Idiopathic avascular necrosis of the capital femoral epiphysis in a child of 4 to 8 years, presenting with painless limp and limited abduction and internal rotation. Containment of the head is the treatment principle.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (risk factor for Perthes disease — male sex, positive family history, passive smoking)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Salter–Harris type I injury involves
options: Separation through the hypertrophic zone of the physis, without a metaphyseal or epiphyseal fragment
A fracture through the metaphysis only
A fracture crossing the physis into the epiphysis
explanation: The hypertrophic zone is the weakest layer. Types I and II spare the germinal layer and have good prognosis; **types IV and V** cross or crush the growth plate and risk growth arrest.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (Salter Harris type 1 fracture involves hypertrophic zone of physis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A fracture line passing through which part of the bone impairs longitudinal growth?
explanation: Longitudinal growth occurs by endochondral ossification at the physis, so damage there causes shortening or angular deformity. Periosteal (appositional) growth increases width only.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (fracture line through which part of bone impairs longitudinal growth — epiphyseal plate)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A supracondylar fracture of the humerus crossing the physis and the joint surface is classified as
explanation: Crossing both the physis and the articular surface requires anatomical reduction and fixation to prevent growth arrest and joint incongruity. Type V is a crush injury recognised only in retrospect.
exam: 2014 AIIMS (supracondylar fracture of humerus — type 4 Salter Harris classification, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Gallows (Bryant) traction is used for
options: Fracture of the femoral shaft in a child under about 2 years or 12 kg
explanation: Both legs are suspended vertically with the buttocks just clear of the bed. The weight limit matters because vascular compromise of the elevated legs can occur in heavier children.
exam: 2024 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (gallows traction is used for fracture shaft of femur, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Congenital pseudoarthrosis most commonly affects which bone, and with which syndrome is it associated?
options: The tibia, associated with neurofibromatosis type 1
The femur, associated with Down syndrome
The clavicle, associated with Marfan syndrome
The radius, associated with Turner syndrome
explanation: Anterolateral bowing of the tibia in infancy progresses to fracture that fails to unite. Treatment is difficult, with vascularised grafting or bone transport, and amputation sometimes needed.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (the given condition is seen in congenital pseudoarthrosis of tibia)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Sprengel deformity is associated with
options: Klippel–Feil syndrome, congenital scoliosis and diastematomyelia
explanation: Sprengel deformity is congenital undescent of the scapula, giving a high small scapula with limited abduction, sometimes tethered by an omovertebral bar. Renal anomalies are also associated.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (Sprengel deformity is associated with Klippel Feil syndrome, congenital scoliosis, diastematomyelia), 2023 INI-CET (match — Klippel Feil syndrome and Sprengel deformity)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis typically presents in
options: An obese adolescent with hip or referred knee pain and the limb held in external rotation
A neonate with a dislocatable hip
An elderly patient after a fall
explanation: The epiphysis slips posteromedially, and Klein line fails to intersect the head on the frontal view. **Knee pain in an adolescent demands examination of the hip**, or the diagnosis is missed.
exam: 2017 AIIMS (Perthes disease risk factors), 2015 AIIMS (Shenton line at the hip)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Genu varum in a toddler that is physiological can be distinguished from Blount disease by
options: Symmetry, absence of a sharp metaphyseal beak, and spontaneous correction by about 2 years of age
The presence of a metaphyseal beak
explanation: Physiological bowing corrects to valgus by age 3. Blount disease shows a sharp medial metaphyseal beak with progressive, often asymmetrical deformity, and rickets must also be excluded.
exam: 2022 NEET-PG (child with bowing of legs — vitamin D deficiency), 2020 INI-CET (CTEV features, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Severe backache with urinary incontinence and intervertebral disc prolapse indicates
explanation: Saddle anaesthesia, bilateral sciatica, reduced anal tone and bladder dysfunction define it. It is a **surgical emergency** requiring urgent MRI and decompression, because delay causes permanent sphincter damage.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (severe backache, urinary incontinence, IV disc prolapse — cauda equina syndrome)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A 65-year-old woman has backache after heavy weight lifting, worse on bending forward, with no neurological deficit. The likely diagnosis is
explanation: Mechanical pain worsened by flexion and relieved by rest, with no red flags, suggests disc disease. Night pain, weight loss, fever, age over 70 with no trauma, or neurological deficit would demand urgent imaging.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (65-year-old with backache and heavy weight lifting, worsens on bending — PIVD, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A young woman has lower backache radiating to the right leg with numbness over the lateral foot and a reduced ankle jerk. The root involved is
explanation: S1 supplies the lateral foot and little toe, powers plantarflexion and mediates the ankle jerk. **L5** affects the dorsum of the foot and great toe with weak dorsiflexion and a normal ankle jerk; **L4** affects the medial leg with a reduced knee jerk.
exam: 2021 NEET-PG (lifting heavy weight, lower backache radiating to right leg — S1)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The normal curvature of the lumbar spine is
explanation: Cervical and lumbar regions are lordotic; thoracic and sacral regions are kyphotic. Lumbar lordosis masks hip flexion deformity, which is why the Thomas test obliterates it first.
exam: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (normal curvature of lumbar spine is lordosis, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: After a road traffic accident a patient has backache and radiographs show reduced anterior vertebral height with an intact posterior wall. The injury is
explanation: Only the anterior column fails, so it is usually stable and managed conservatively. A **burst** fracture involves the posterior wall with retropulsion and risks canal compromise; a Chance fracture is a flexion-distraction injury.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (RTA with backache, X-ray showing decrease in anterior height of vertebra — compression fracture)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Chronic low back pain with mild forward slippage of L5 over S1 on imaging is
explanation: Meyerding grades it by the percentage of slip. **Spondylolysis** is a pars interarticularis defect without slip, often in young athletes; spondylosis is degenerative change.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (chronic low back pain with slippage of L5 over S1 — spondylolisthesis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Removal of a vertebral disc can be performed by all EXCEPT
explanation: Laminoplasty **reconstructs and expands** the canal, typically in cervical myelopathy, rather than providing access for discectomy. Microdiscectomy through a laminotomy window is the usual modern approach.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (removal of vertebral disc can be done by laminotomy, laminectomy, hemilaminectomy, not laminoplasty)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Scoliosis requiring surgical correction in a growing adolescent is generally a Cobb angle above
explanation: Curves under 20 degrees are observed and 20 to 40 degrees braced while growth continues. Risser sign grades skeletal maturity and predicts progression; adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is the commonest type.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (angle of scoliosis — Cobb's angle)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Lumbar canal stenosis is distinguished from vascular claudication by
options: Pain relieved by sitting or spinal flexion, with preserved peripheral pulses
explanation: Flexion widens the canal, producing the "shopping trolley" posture. Vascular claudication is relieved simply by stopping, regardless of position, and the pulses are diminished.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (backache worsening on bending — PIVD, 2X), 2024 INI-CET (cauda equina syndrome)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: In tuberculosis of the spine, the deformity that develops with progressive vertebral collapse is
explanation: Anterior vertebral body destruction with a preserved posterior column produces the angular deformity. Paraplegia may occur early from abscess and oedema, or late from fibrosis and bony ridging.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (paradiscal Pott's spine involvement), 2023 INI-CET (ankylosing spondylitis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy is suggested by
options: A spastic gait with hyperreflexia below the level of compression and a positive Hoffmann sign
explanation: Clumsy hands, loss of dexterity and gait disturbance are early features. MRI is the investigation of choice and surgical decompression prevents progression, as recovery of established deficit is limited.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (laminoplasty and canal expansion), 2024 INI-CET (cauda equina syndrome)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Forceps with a serrated margin on one side and a smooth margin on the other, used in fracture fixation, are
explanation: The serrated jaw grips the bone while the smooth jaw holds the plate without damaging it. Bone-holding (Lane or Fergusson) forceps instead have two serrated jaws for gripping bone alone.
exam: 2024 INI-CET (forceps with serrated margin on one side and smooth on other — plate holding forceps), 2014 AIIMS (identify the instrument — bone holding forceps)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A bone nibbler is used to
options: Remove fibrous tissue and sclerotic bone from a non-union site
explanation: Freshening the bone ends restores a bleeding surface for union. Rongeurs, curettes and osteotomes serve related functions, and bone grafting usually follows.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (bone nibbler is used to remove fibrous tissue from non-union site)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Instruments needed for skeletal traction through the tibia include
options: Steinmann pin, Denham pin, Bohler stirrup and Bohler–Braun frame
Kirschner wire and tension band wire only
Dynamic hip screw and guide wire
explanation: A Denham pin has a central thread that grips bone and resists sliding. The pin is inserted from the **lateral** side of the tibia to avoid the common peroneal nerve, 2 cm below and behind the tubercle.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (instruments needed for skeletal traction in tibia — Steinmann's pin, Denham's pin, Bohler stirrup, Bohler Braun frame)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Arrange external fixator configurations in increasing order of stability.
options: Uniplanar one rod → uniplanar two rods → biplanar → circular (ring) fixator
Circular → biplanar → uniplanar two rods → uniplanar one rod
explanation: Stability increases with more pins, more planes and shorter bone-to-rod distance. The Ilizarov ring fixator is the most stable and allows distraction osteogenesis and deformity correction.
exam: 2023 INI-CET (arrange the following in order of stability — uniplanar with one rod, two rods, biplanar)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A spanning external fixator is used for
options: A periarticular fracture about the knee, bridging the joint temporarily
explanation: It maintains length and alignment while soft tissue swelling settles, as part of staged management — the same principle as in Pilon fractures. Definitive internal fixation follows.
exam: 2023 NEET-PG (spanning external fixator is used for periarticular fracture knee, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A comminuted fracture of the lower end of the femur can be stabilised by
options: A rail (monolateral) fixator or bridge plating
explanation: Comminuted metaphyseal fractures are treated by **relative** stability, spanning the zone of comminution without disturbing the fragments, so that secondary bone healing by callus occurs.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (comminuted fracture in lower end of femur stabilised by rail fixator)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Application of a compression plate to a diaphyseal fracture leads to
options: Primary bone healing, without visible callus
explanation: Absolute stability with interfragmentary compression permits direct osteonal remodelling through cutting cones. **Relative** stability from nails and bridge plates instead produces callus-mediated secondary healing.
exam: 2019 NEET-PG (application of a plate on a diaphyseal fracture leads to primary healing of fracture)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Callus formation at a fracture site is increased by
options: Small repeated movements at the fracture site
explanation: Micromotion stimulates periosteal callus and cartilage formation, which is why nailed fractures show abundant callus. **Excessive** motion or distraction instead causes non-union, so the stimulus must be controlled.
exam: 2016 AIIMS (growth of cartilage following fracture increased by repeated tiny movements at fracture site), 2015 AIIMS (which increases callus formation — movement at fracture site)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: In an intertrochanteric femoral fracture, one-year morbidity is reduced by
options: Early internal fixation with early mobilisation
explanation: Prolonged recumbency causes pneumonia, pressure sores, thromboembolism and deconditioning, which drive mortality rather than the fracture itself. A dynamic hip screw or cephalomedullary nail is used.
exam: 2020 INI-CET (in intertrochanteric fracture femur, one year morbidity can be reduced — true)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The ideal treatment for a distal radius fracture with sharp fragment ends threatening the skin and nerve is
options: Neurological assessment, closed reduction, then repeat neurological assessment
explanation: Documenting neurovascular status **before and after** any manipulation is the principle, because reduction itself can cause or relieve nerve injury and the sequence determines liability and management.
exam: 2020 NEET-PG (ideal treatment for distal radius fracture with sharp ends — neurological assessment, closed reduction, again neurological assessment)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Structures divided during a fasciotomy are
options: Skin, subcutaneous fat, superficial fascia and deep fascia
Skin and deep fascia only, leaving the superficial fascia intact
explanation: The deep fascia is the constricting layer, but the skin itself becomes constricting once swelling is severe, so skin incisions must be generous and are left open for delayed closure or grafting.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (structures cut in fasciotomy — skin, subcutaneous fat, superficial fascia, deep fascia)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: The earliest sign of compartment syndrome that a nurse can detect in a patient with a limb fracture is
options: Excessive pain not relieved by the usual dose of analgesia
explanation: Pain out of proportion to the injury, worsened by passive stretch of the compartment muscles, is the earliest and most reliable sign. **Pulselessness and paralysis are late** and indicate established damage.
exam: 2021 INI-CET / 2014 AIIMS (earliest way to detect compartment syndrome — excessive pain not relieved by usual dose of analgesics, 3X), 2019 NEET-PG (which finding appears late in compartment syndrome — paralysis)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Compartment syndrome is most commonly associated with
options: Supracondylar fracture of the humerus and fractures of the tibia
explanation: Both involve tight fascial compartments close to major vessels. Untreated forearm ischaemia causes **Volkmann contracture**, with fixed flexion of the wrist and fingers from muscle fibrosis.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (compartment syndrome is commonly seen with supracondylar fracture of humerus — answer not recorded in source)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: A patient with a femoral shaft fracture develops breathlessness, confusion and a petechial rash 12 hours after injury. The diagnosis is
explanation: Gurd criteria require hypoxia, neurological change and a petechial rash, typically 24 to 72 hours after a long bone fracture — earlier than thromboembolism. Early fracture fixation and supportive care are the management.
exam: 2023 INI-CET / 2019 NEET-PG (shaft of femur fracture with SOB 12 hours later and confusion — fat embolism, 2X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Avascular necrosis is a recognised risk after fracture of all EXCEPT
explanation: Avascular necrosis follows injury where the blood supply is retrograde and single-source — femoral head, scaphoid proximal pole, talus, humeral head and lunate. The clavicle has a rich periosteal supply and unites readily.
exam: 2018 AIIMS (proximal 1/3 of scaphoid susceptible to avascular necrosis), 2023 INI-CET (avascular necrosis of femoral head, 3X)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Myositis ossificans traumatica is
options: Heterotopic bone formation in a muscle haematoma after injury, classically at the elbow
explanation: It follows supracondylar fracture or elbow dislocation, particularly after repeated forceful passive manipulation — which is why vigorous physiotherapy early after elbow injury is avoided.
exam: 2022 INI-CET (supracondylar fracture of humerus and three bony points, 3X), 2018 AIIMS (intra-articular fracture features)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Non-union of a fracture is most reliably distinguished from delayed union by
options: Absence of any progression towards healing over three consecutive months with a sclerotic, sealed medullary canal
explanation: Hypertrophic non-union reflects excess motion with adequate blood supply and needs stability; atrophic non-union reflects poor vascularity and needs bone graft as well.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (bone nibbler for non-union site), 2016 AIIMS (movement at fracture site increasing callus)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Complex regional pain syndrome after a fracture is characterised by
options: Pain disproportionate to the injury with vasomotor, sudomotor and trophic changes
explanation: Allodynia, swelling, colour and temperature change, altered sweating and later stiffness and osteoporosis occur. Early mobilisation, physiotherapy, neuropathic analgesia and sometimes sympathetic blockade are used.
exam: 2021 INI-CET (compartment syndrome detection, 3X), 2020 NEET-PG (distal radius fracture management)

subject: Orthopedics
stem: Volkmann ischaemic contracture results from
options: Untreated forearm compartment syndrome causing muscle necrosis and fibrosis with fixed flexion of the wrist and fingers
explanation: Flexor digitorum profundus is affected most, so finger flexion deformity improves on wrist flexion — the Volkmann sign. Prevention by timely fasciotomy is the only effective management.
exam: 2018 NEET-PG (vessel affected in supracondylar fracture — brachial artery, 2X), 2021 INI-CET (compartment syndrome, 3X)
